big_case_rationale: Marquee free-exercise case on Smith's general-applicability standard at the religion/LGBTQ-nondiscrimination seam of a universal school-choice program; SG amicus support, a multistate amicus bloc, and 30+ merits amici mark it as one of the Term's most watched.

semantic_claims.proposition: The majority will rest the judgment on Employment Division v. Smith's general-applicability prong as glossed by Fulton v. City of Philadelphia and Tandon v. Newsom: it will hold that Colorado's equal-opportunity condition is not generally applicable because the program's categorical and discretionary secular carve-outs (e.g., providers serving only low-income children, children with disabilities, or specified identity groups) undermine the State's asserted nondiscrimination interests in a manner comparable to the religious exemption petitioners seek, expressly rejecting the Tenth Circuit's rule that only 'unfettered' discretion or exemptions for 'identical' secular conduct defeat general applicability; applying strict scrutiny, it will hold the exclusion of the Catholic preschools unconstitutional. The majority will not overrule Smith and will not rest the holding on Carson v. Makin's status-based-exclusion rule (QP2).

The majority will state its ground as a categorical rule, not a fact-bound one: a comparability standard for general applicability that governs any exemption-bearing scheme or public-benefit program — a law fails Smith's general-applicability prong whenever its secular exceptions, categorical or discretionary, undermine the government's interests comparably to the requested religious accommodation — rather than a holding confined to Colorado's preschool program, to education funding, or to these parties. Its breadth will stop at existing doctrine: the Court will decline to revisit Smith itself, leaving rational-basis review for genuinely neutral and generally applicable laws intact.
